Any games, game series or companies that seem to both innovate too much and be stale at the same time?
Assassin's creed I guess. They add new things with every game but it still feels repetitive. I think that series needs more puzzle elements in it.
pretty much any open world Ubisoft game. They all start feeling the same.

Tripwire Interactive. They brought all sorts of new things to the table, like making (arguably) the first FPS where you can aim down sights (Red Orchestra), the first true 3D scope (Red Orchestra again), being heavily opposed to the idea of a crosshair (until they tried pandering to the CoD crowd in Red Orchestra 2, which backfired horribly), first person tank interiors with players acting as crewmembers rather than "being" the tank (Red Orchestra 2), realistic tank damage models (Red Orchestra 2 again), persistent gore (Killing Floor 2), suppression (Red Orchestra 2) and probably some more that I'm missing.

Why are they stale? Because as far as pure game design goes, they are inexperienced at best. All they can think of to make a game more replayable is adding grinding. +0.5% to all stats per level sounds fine, until you realise there are like a hundred levels, at which point older players have massive advantages over new ones, as if the game wasn't difficult enough to pick up already (Red Orchestra 2). Then there's the tiering system in Killing Floor which encourages people to kick newer players not cause they are bad, but cause even if they play perfectly their stats alone hinder the team; I don't blame people for doing it, having a couple of low-level characters in your team at a high difficulty is suicide, the game is just designed that stupidly. They use progression systems even if they make the game worse.

Let's not forget to mention all the things they promised but never delivered in Red Orchestra 2 (co-op campaign, several tanks and other vehicles per side, dealing with griefers, rare weapons actually being rare), and most important of all, the CEO's and lead designer's classic line when questioned about historical accuracy, "it's good enough for me".
Nintendo. The issue with them is that they rely too much on gimmicks. (EDIT: while too often not providing actual innovation.)
